name: Thallus of Miletus
bio: Thallus of Miletus is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 1st century AD. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of the Wreath of Philippus, the Garland compiled in the first century AD.
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the first volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Books I–VI) (Book VI: 91, 235).

poems.title: Book VI, 91
poems.author: Thallus of Miletus
poems.text: The shield is the offering of Promachus, the spears of Aconteus, the sword of Eumedes, and this bow is Cydon’s. Hippomedon offers the reins, Melantas the helmet, Nico the greaves, Aristomachus the pike, and Philinus the cuirass. Grant to them ail, Ares, spoiler of men, ever to win trophies from the foemen.

poems.title: Book VI, 235
poems.author: Thallus of Miletus
poems.text: Caesar, offspring of the unconquered race of Romulus, joy of the farthest East and West, we sing thy divine birth, and round the altars pour glad libations to the gods. But mayest thou, treading in thy grandsire’s steps, abide with us, even as we pray, for many years.
